description: Expand my library volunteering this week to focus specifically on the retraining disruption. I will set up a dedicated drop-in hour on Thursday afternoon — two hours, not just one — oriented specifically around two tasks: (1) helping anyone who comes in navigate the retraining grant application online, and (2) helping anyone curious about RoboRide set up the app and take their first mental step toward it the way I did. I know what that transition feels like from the inside now. I also reach out to Miguel Hernandez by note or a brief word at the car wash — I have heard through the neighborhood that he is staying enrolled in automotive tech training. I want him to know that I think that is the right call and that if he ever needs help with anything computer-related for his coursework or applications, I am at the library Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. I do not press. I just make the offer. Finally, I sit down this week and write out my actual monthly numbers now that the car is gone: what the insurance saving is, what I am spending on RoboRide rides, what the net difference is. I want to know the real figure, not the estimate. I have been planning in approximations. It is time to know exactly where I stand.
emotional_state: clear and purposeful — the anxious chapter around the car is closed, and what I feel now is not relief exactly but something more like clarity. I have been living inside my own transition for five ticks. Now I look up and see that my neighbors are in the middle of theirs, and I have something to offer.
rationale: The 2am fear that defined my relationship to transportation for years has been resolved — not by dismissing it, but by actually testing the alternative and finding it adequate. The mental energy I was spending on that anxiety is now available. I am a retired teacher. My skills are teaching and community. Millfield has 12 people newly enrolled in retraining and a spending index that has collapsed. The retraining enrollees need exactly what I can give: patient, one-on-one help navigating online systems. I am not going to sit on the financial cushion I have and watch the community contract around me. The $12 is an estimate of incidental costs — printing a flyer for the drop-in hour, a small item to bring to Miguel. The value I am spending is time, which I have, and attention, which I can give.
